patch.value: Recursive self-improvement loop: the immutable record selects, gates, and re-measures the next improvement to pm itself, so each cycle proves a number moved

A declared cycle exists — observe, propose, gate, land, re-measure — whose every turn is a tracked item carrying a receipt naming the metric, the baseline, and the post-change value; Candidate selection is derived from evidence already in the record rather than from filing recency; Every shipped cycle can answer, from tracked data alone, whether pm got better and by how much; The loop composes the existing measurement surfaces rather than duplicating them: the population ratchet, the defect-recurrence gate, the escape ratchet, the dogfood ratchet, trajectory projection, and the token corpus

value.text:
Duplicate check before filing (2026-08-05): searched the full corpus for recursive self improvement, self-improvement loops, and 'pm improves itself using its own tracker data'. The hits are all narrower and all real neighbours rather than duplicates — pm-cc04 is an ADR for agent self-repair through a remediation registry, pm-dhrp was a validation auto-fix session, pm-0682l4 and pm-k9t17l are self-reference guards in install and ordering. Nothing composes the measurement surfaces into a cycle.

What exists is substrate, not a loop: pm-ips23h ratchets filed populations so they cannot grow, pm-1qkivy turns resolved incident patterns into gates, pm-rtn5h6 requires every escaped defect to land the gate that would have caught it, pm-pww8ax ratchets dogfood coverage, pm-qd6gvf projects the record as trajectories, pm-8pnj measures tokens per completed task, pm-2vs1za compares measured cost against forecast value. Each answers one question about one pass. None answers 'is pm getting better, by how much, measured how' across passes.

The asymmetry that motivates the ledger child: a ceiling can only ever prove a number did not grow. Every measurement the project ratchets is therefore blind to improvement — the one direction the loop needs to observe.

value.text: Recursive improvement operating model. Observe from immutable measurements, defect recurrence, release incidents, user friction, token cost, graph bottlenecks, and evaluation failures. Synthesize a ranked candidate with evidence, uncertainty, expected value, blast radius, and a falsifiable metric hypothesis. Materialize the candidate as a canonical item after all-status duplicate and lineage checks; generate a bounded implementation and verification plan; execute only inside the authority and sandbox declared by that item; run local and hosted gates against the exact change; then compare the same metric definition and corpus before and after. Land, reject, or revert based on the declared threshold, never on narrative confidence, and store the full receipt and trajectory so the next cycle can learn from both success and failure. Anti-Goodhart constraints require invariant safety and feature-parity gates, held-out evaluation scenarios, no ratchet weakening, and explicit accounting for displaced cost. The loop may propose work autonomously but cannot expand authority, bypass review or release policy, fabricate dependencies, or mutate history outside normal SDK primitives.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Recursive improvement control loop: observe immutable operational, quality, token, latency, reliability, security, and user/agent outcome measures; attribute candidate causes from typed history and recurrence families; propose a bounded change with explicit hypothesis, affected population, cost, rollback-by-new-event plan, and protected invariants; rank it against alternatives and no-change; execute in an isolated branch/environment; run repository-owned negative controls, held-out evals, counterfactual replay, and exact-artifact checks; land only when the causal metric target improves without protected-metric regression; then remeasure production and feed the result back as append-only evidence. Separate proposer, evaluator, and policy authority so the system cannot approve its own unobserved claims. Use sequential tests or confidence intervals for noisy metrics, change-point detection for regressions, Pareto/frontier decisions for multi-objective tradeoffs, and explicit cost displacement so token savings that move cost elsewhere do not count as improvement. Guard against Goodhart behavior with rotating held-out suites, contamination/leakage checks, human policy constraints, population-adequacy proofs, novelty caps, and stop conditions. Every cycle is reproducible from SDK events and can be restored or reversed only by a new compensating event; no history rewrite, silent waiver, non-terminal external check, or unverifiable model judgment is treated as success.
